title: Life Is a Span, — a Fleeting Hour
description: Life Is a Span, — a Fleeting Hour in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 584 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Death of a Child”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Life is a span, a fleet-ing hour: How soon the va-por flies! Man is a ten-der, tran-sient flower, That e'en in bloom-ing dies.

lines: Life is a span, — a fleeting hour:
Man is a tender, transient flower,
The once-loved form, now cold and dead,
And nature weeps, her comforts fled,
Hope looks beyond the bounds of time,
Shall rise in full, immortal prime,
And bloom to fade no more.
Cease, then, fond nature, cease thy tears;

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
